solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put one's foot in it — small gardening tool?

definitions.note: read as a description: the thing into which one puts one's foot

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a hoe is a long-handled tool for weeding

explanation.surface: Someone blunders socially, then asks about a little tool for the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's foot in it' looks like the idiom for a blunder, but read literally it describes footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear is literally the item you insert your foot into, a playful literal reading of the idiom.

clue.text: Initially having appeared, lax, vague even, share equally

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Something vague and lax has turned up, and two people are told to split it between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide something into two equal parts is to split it fifty-fifty.

clue.text: Animal's name the panel worked out

definitions.note: read as 'Animal is', with the 's as the link to the wordplay

indicators.note: letters that are worked out are solved like a puzzle, so the words the panel are rearranged

explanation.surface: A panel of judges has finally identified an animal's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The big grey tusked mammal of Africa and Asia is a well-known animal.

clue.text: See about the Italian, overindulged

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the word for see goes round the Italian article

parts.note: to spot something is to see it
il is the Italian for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone notices an Italian who has been pampered.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilt child is one who has been pampered and given too much.

clue.text: Describing distinctive cultural group of 100 — cite changes allowing 50 in

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: allowing ... in means letting something enter, so the numeral goes inside
with allowing, in signals that one piece goes inside the other
changes tells us the letters of cite are reshuffled

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: An awkward description of a cultural group of a hundred people, with citations altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' turns CITE into ETIC, and 'allowing 50 in' puts L inside it to make ELTIC, after C.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective refers to peoples such as the Irish, Scots, Welsh and Bretons, a distinct cultural family.

clue.text: Poem on river — European one

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A poet writes verse about a river somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European one' means a European river, picking up 'river' from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder flows through the Czech Republic, Poland and Germany to the Baltic Sea.

clue.text: "Guy in charge is entertaining island pair" I see what you're saying

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so the leader word goes around the other letters

parts.note: the person in charge is the leader

explanation.surface: A quoted remark about a boss hosting a couple from an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I see what you're saying' is normally an idiom for understanding; here it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A deaf person who follows speech by watching mouth movements could literally say they see what is said.

clue.text: Referring to country version of rugby — endless criticism follows

indicators.note: follows means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: RU stands for rugby union, one of the two codes of rugby

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for criticism is cut off

parts.note: stick is informal British for criticism, as in 'getting stick'

explanation.surface: A rural version of rugby attracts nonstop criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' in British slang means harsh criticism; lose its last letter to get STIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things of the countryside, simple and rural in style.

clue.text: Conservative not happy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... is the colour of the UK Conservative Party, so a Tory is a ...
second meaning: feeling down or sad

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a gloomy Tory; the two words are separate senses of one colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour stands for the Tory party in Britain and also for low spirits, as in having the blues.

clue.text: Shrub inapt? Dreadfully — this might add colour

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of shrub and inapt are muddled

explanation.surface: A shrub planted in the wrong place looks terrible, and something might brighten it up.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's tool with bristles is used to apply paint, so it adds colour to a surface.

clue.text: Become entangled in some shrubbery

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words some shrubbery

explanation.surface: Someone gets caught up in a patch of bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears or nets that interlock or tangle together are said to engage this way, a verb sense of netting.

clue.text: CIA at court unusually, laying down the law?

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of CIA at court are arranged in an uncommon way

explanation.surface: The CIA in a courtroom behaving oddly while the judge hands down rulings.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictatorial ruler imposes rules on everyone, which is figuratively laying down the law.

clue.text: Choose page in Old Testament

indicators.note: in means the page letter is placed inside the scripture abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone selects a page from the Old Testament to read.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to make a selection or decision between alternatives.

clue.text: Surprise a lot when weight is heavy at the outset

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a ton is a unit of weight

indicators.note: at the outset means only the first letter of heavy is used

explanation.surface: A big surprise arrives when a heavy weight is lifted at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' belongs with 'Surprise' in the definition, not to the wordplay as a large amount.
explanation.definitionFit: To amaze someone is to surprise them greatly.

clue.text: Fertilizer container, for example, hot

parts.note: a pot is a container
as can mean for example, as in 'trees, as oak'
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a fertiliser by its pot and its warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium compounds of this name are widely spread on fields as plant food.

clue.text: Competitor making no changes to accommodate temperature and energy

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so the word for unchanging holds the two letters

parts.note: something constant stays the same and does not change
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A competitor sticks to the routine regardless of heat or tiredness.
explanation.definitionFit: A participant in a quiz or competition is a competitor.

clue.text: Proper elm? Yes, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected result, so the letters of elm and yes are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is asked whether an elm tree is proper and answers yes, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemly behaviour is decorous and fitting, so it is proper.

clue.text: Supply a horse for riding

parts.note: a mount is a horse that is ridden

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to provide a horse to ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a verb meaning provide, but it is a noun, a quantity held.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply of something is a quantity or total of it, as in a store of goods.

clue.text: Tutor always holding test

indicators.note: holding means the words Tutor always contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: A teacher who is forever setting examinations.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken examination, especially in languages, is a kind of test.

clue.text: Change beer? About time! Right

indicators.note: about means around, so the beer word goes round the time letter

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A drinker demands a different beer, exasperated it has taken so long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time!' reads as an exclamation of impatience, but 'About' is the containment signal and 'time' is T.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to modify it.

clue.text: Worker by sea with personal clothing

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea
something your own is personal to you

explanation.surface: A labourer by the seaside carrying their own clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments passed on from an older sibling are second-hand clothing.

clue.text: Party, extremely grandiose, for Venice magistrate

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: extremely points to the outermost letters of grandiose

explanation.surface: A lavish party is thrown for a Venetian official.
explanation.definitionFit: The doge was the chief elected magistrate who ruled the old Venetian republic.

clue.text: Very small quantity of iron that's taken regularly

indicators.note: taken regularly means every other letter of iron that is picked out

explanation.surface: A tiny dose of iron supplement is taken daily.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest Greek letter's name has come to mean a tiny amount or jot.

clue.text: Cheerful, puts down in part of Scotland

parts.note: high can mean elated or in good spirits
an aircraft lands when it puts down

explanation.surface: A happy traveller touches down in the north of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountainous northern region of Scotland is known by this name.

clue.text: Lady's love for principal character

parts.note: her is the possessive for a lady, as in 'her book'
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman's sweetheart is the main figure in her story.
explanation.definitionFit: The protagonist of a novel or film is its central figure.
